items.prompt: The frontend's Complete button sends PUT /api/tasks/1 with the body { "completed": true }. What does the committed backend answer?
items.answer: 400 Validation failed: PUT parses with createTaskSchema, which needs a title
distractors: 200 with the task marked completed: PUT accepts a partial set of the task's fields
404 Task not found: the update service swallows the validation error
500 Failed to update task: completed is not a known database column
items.explanation: PUT reuses createTaskSchema (title: z.string().min(1)). A body without title fails parse, the ZodError branch returns 400. The README's 'Before You Try to Run It' list calls this out.

items.prompt: A client works around the bug by sending PUT with { "title": "Same title", "completed": true }. What happens to the task's completed flag?
items.answer: It stays unchanged: validation passes, but Zod strips the unknown completed key
distractors: It becomes true: the title requirement is now satisfied and completed is passed on
The request fails with 400: completed is an unrecognized key in the schema
It becomes true: the schema keeps completed but resets the title to an empty default
items.explanation: z.object() drops keys it does not declare by default; createTaskSchema declares only title, description and dueDate. PHASE2 0.2 points out this second, quieter failure.

items.prompt: tasks.ts defines updateTaskSchema = createTaskSchema.partial(). Where is it used?
items.answer: Nowhere: it is defined, but the PUT handler still parses with createTaskSchema
distractors: In the PUT handler: that is why a partial update carrying only completed works
In the POST handler: creating a task with no title at all is therefore allowed
In a separate PATCH handler: the frontend's Complete button calls it instead of PUT
items.explanation: There is no PATCH route at all, and PUT calls createTaskSchema.parse. Even switching to updateTaskSchema would still strip completed, because partial() keeps the same declared keys.

items.prompt: Postgres is stopped and a client sends DELETE /api/tasks/1. What status does the committed backend return?
items.answer: 404 Task not found: deleteTask catches every error and returns false
distractors: 500 Failed to delete task: the route's own catch block sends that status
503 Service Unavailable: Prisma reports the database as being down
204 No Content: the delete is queued until the database comes back
items.explanation: The bare catch in deleteTask converts a connection failure into false; the route's catch never sees an exception. PHASE2 0.3 asks you to catch only P2025 and rethrow the rest.

items.prompt: updateTask spreads data and then sets dueDate: data.dueDate ? new Date(data.dueDate) : undefined. When the request omits dueDate, what happens to the stored due date?
items.answer: It is left unchanged: Prisma treats an undefined update field as 'do not touch'
distractors: It is cleared to NULL: undefined is written into the column as a missing value
It is set to the current time: the fallback branch calls new Date() for it
The update fails: dueDate is required whenever any update data is sent
items.explanation: In Prisma, undefined means the field is omitted from the update, while null would clear it. createTask, by contrast, writes null explicitly when no dueDate is given.

items.prompt: POST /api/tasks with { "title": "Read docs" } and no dueDate. What is stored in the new row's dueDate column?
items.answer: NULL: createTask maps a missing dueDate to null, which DateTime? accepts
distractors: The creation timestamp: createdAt is copied over whenever no due date is supplied
An Invalid Date: new Date(undefined) is still called for the column
Nothing is stored: the request fails validation without a dueDate
items.explanation: The ternary only constructs a Date when a dueDate string was sent. dueDate is optional in both the Zod schema and the Prisma model.

items.prompt: In what order does GET /api/tasks return tasks?
items.answer: Newest first, as getAllTasks orders by createdAt descending
distractors: By id ascending, the default order the database returns rows in
Incomplete tasks first, then completed ones, each by title
By dueDate, soonest first, with undated tasks at the end
items.explanation: findMany is called with orderBy: { createdAt: 'desc' }. There is no pagination or filtering yet; PHASE2 section 2 adds them.

items.prompt: Why does the committed backend fail before it ever serves a request?
items.answer: index.ts imports cors, but no cors entry is listed in backend/package.json dependencies
distractors: The Prisma schema has no Task model, so the Prisma client cannot be generated at install
PORT is required in the environment and has no default value in index.ts
express.json() is never registered, so the startup validation step fails
items.explanation: Dependencies list only @prisma/client, express and zod. PHASE2 0.1 adds cors and @types/cors (and a DATABASE_URL in .env) as the first exercise.

items.prompt: When the backend answers the Complete request with 400 { error, details }, what does the frontend's updateTask(id, data) resolve to?
items.answer: undefined: fetch does not reject on a 400, and the error body has no data field
distractors: It rejects with the 400 status code: the mutation's onError handler runs instead
The error object: json.data falls back to the whole response body
It never resolves: the error response body is never consumed
items.explanation: updateTask never checks res.ok. A failed update therefore looks like a successful mutation that returned nothing - one reason the Complete bug is easy to miss in the UI.

items.prompt: What does a successful DELETE /api/tasks/:id send back?
items.answer: Status 204 and an empty response body
distractors: Status 200 with { data: deletedTask }
Status 202 with { status: 'queued' }
Status 200 with { data: true } as JSON
items.explanation: res.status(204).send() - No Content. Every other success in this router returns a { data } envelope.

items.answer: JSON with status 'ok' and the current timestamp as an ISO string
distractors: JSON with status 'ok' and the current database connection state
The plain text OK with a 200 status and no JSON body
JSON with the current task count and the server's uptime in seconds
items.explanation: The handler never touches the database, so it reports process liveness only - a Postgres outage still answers ok.

items.front: Why should updateTask/deleteTask catch only Prisma error P2025 instead of every error?
items.back: P2025 is 'record not found' - the only failure that truly means 404. Catching everything turns outages and bugs into 404s; rethrowing the rest lets the route answer 500.

items.front: In grokbuildjs, what belongs in routes/ versus services/?
items.back: Routes own HTTP concerns: validation, status codes, response shape. Services own business logic and Prisma data access, so they can be tested and swapped independently.

items.front: What response envelope does the tasks router promise for success and for errors?
items.back: Success: { data: ... }. Error: { error: "message", details?: ... } - one consistent shape the frontend can rely on.
